newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey says expects fall in H2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Plessey says expects fall in H2 earnings.

text.p: Electronics company Plessey Corp Ltd said on Friday that it expectecd second half earnings to be below those of the first half and for the previous year.
It said the reasons for the expected fall in results were that the sale of a non-branded television business unit had been reversed after the purchasers failed to meet their obligations.

"This together with lower sales and margins in the television and audio business had led to worse than expected results in the consumer electronics division," the company said in a cautionary announcement.
It said the future of this division was currently under review.
At the time of its interim results last November, the company said it anticipated an improved performance in the second half of the year.

The company's chairman and managing director's review had foreseen uncertainty in the telecommunications market, while its interim statement had foreseen increasing sales in communications during the half year.

"These did occur but due to pressure arising from the phasing of deliveries and installations this business was not able to deliver sufficient earnings to compensate for the shortfalls caused by the consumer division," it said.
The directors remained confident in the medium to longer terms prospects of the company.
Shareholders were advised to exercise caution in their sharedealings until the company's annual results were announced in May.

Plessey shares were last trading at 770 cents each on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange -- their lowest level since November 17 1995 -- and have fallen 230 cents since February 11 when they were quoted at 1,000 cents each.
